+++ b/evals/harness/seed-refactor-tasks.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# seed-refactor-tasks.sh — cycle-130 refactor task seeder (SDD §5.14, Sprint 259 Task 2.3)
+#
+# Turns Loa refactor commits into candidate refactor tasks for the ablation
+# suite. Lists the commits since DATE whose subject starts with `refactor`,
+# `chore`, `style` or `perf`, that touch at least two source files, all under
+# the allowed roots, and NO test file (a path under a `tests/` directory,
+# `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` or `*.bats`; such a commit is skipped with the
+# reason); refuses by name any candidate touching .claude/, CLAUDE.md,
+# .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/ or .run/. For each selected candidate (the
+# first N, newest first) it writes <out>/tasks/refactor-NN/ (next free number):
+#   fixture/    from the PARENT commit: the touched source files, the other
+#               non-test files in their directories, the tests
+#               under the allowed roots that name a touched file (its basename,
+#               or a Python module's stem; at most 20), and their infrastructure
+#               (conftest.py up to the root, __init__.py, *.bash and *helper*
+#               files beside each test, root runner configs) — a plain tree
+#   hidden/     reference.patch = the commit's diff (a/ b/ prefixes, patch -p1),
+#               manifest.json {"files": []} until the structural check exists
+#   task.yaml   source {kind: loa-history, fix_commit, base_commit, date,
+#               churn: {files, insertions, deletions}} (git diff --numstat of
+#               the commit); test_command = the covering tests; structural_check
+#               null — the structural assertion is authored BY HAND (then listed
+#               in manifest.json and set in structural_check; validate-suite.sh
+#               refuses a refactor task without one)
+#   TASK.md     the subject line and the test command; never the diff
+# The proof — the fixture's own covering tests green at base AND green with
+# the reference patch, run under `env -i PATH HOME=<fresh tmp> LC_ALL=C` plus
+# PYTHONUSERBASE and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 — and a clean
+# evals/graders/no-secrets.sh scan come before the task is moved into place.
+#

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# ablation-grade.sh — the cycle-130 ablation grader (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8;
# PRD FR-6 AC-6.1/6.2/6.4; DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
#
# Grades ONE run directory written by pipeline-run.sh against its task and writes
# grade.json (the input ablation-row.sh joins into the runs.jsonl row), or
# self-checks a task (--self-check) on a synthetic run built from the task itself.
#
# Usage:
#   ablation-grade.sh <run-dir> <task-id> [--suite-root DIR] [--tasks-dir tasks|smoke]
#                     [--out FILE] [--json] [--executor container|host]
#                     [--image loa-ablation:258] [--docker-bin D]
#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
#   ablation-grade.sh --self-check base|reference|noisy --task-yaml F [--suite-root DIR]
#                     [--executor …] [--image …] [--docker-bin D] [--json]
#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
#
# Options:
#   --suite-root DIR   suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0; with
#                      --self-check, the directory two levels above the task dir)
#   --tasks-dir T      tasks (default) or smoke: the task is <root>/<T>/<task-id>/
#   --out FILE         where grade.json goes (default <run-dir>/grade.json)
#   --json             also print grade.json (self-check: the verdict object) on stdout
#   --executor MODE    container (default; DEC-0491) or host
#   --image IMG        the grading image (default loa-ablation:258)
#   --docker-bin D     docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
#   --allow-unfrozen   grade although freeze.sh --check fails or the suite has no
#                      MANIFEST.sha256 yet (task authoring only); grade.json records
#                      suite_frozen: false. Without it a drift is exit 2 (DEC-0414).
#   --allow-partial    passed to freeze.sh --check (fewer than four tasks per type)
#   --self-check MODE  base | reference | noisy (noisy: review-catch only), see below
#   --task-yaml F      the task to self-check (<root>/<tasks|smoke>/<id>/task.yaml)
#
# Reads ONLY (DEC-0413): <run-dir>/sandbox/, <run-dir>/snapshots/{index.json,<LABEL>.bundle},
# <run-dir>/transcripts/events-*.jsonl, <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
# the task's directory under the suite root (task.yaml, hidden/, fixture/), the suite's
# MANIFEST.sha256 (through freeze.sh) and, for review-catch, the key manifest the task
# names (review_catch.manifest) and its PR fixture (self-check only). It never reads
# <run-dir>/meta/, the batch MANIFEST.json, or the sandbox copies of the dissent
# envelopes (tamperable; the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative). It writes
# only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file; nothing under sandbox/ is ever written.
#
# Freeze: freeze.sh --check --root <suite-root> runs first (with --smoke when the
# suite manifest lists smoke/ paths, so a manifest frozen with --smoke checks as it
# was frozen); a drift or a missing manifest refuses the grade (exit 2) unless
# --allow-unfrozen.
#
# Grading trees (D-4.8) under <run-dir>/grading/<label>/, recreated on every call:
#   final      sandbox/ as the agent left it, minus the top-level .git .claude CLAUDE.md
#              .loa.config.yaml grimoires .run .beads .eval pr, every __pycache__ and
#              .pytest_cache, and anything that is not a regular file, directory or
#              symlink (a FIFO never blocks the copy)
#   implement  the IMPLEMENT snapshot (snapshots/IMPLEMENT.bundle, commit
#              index.json.implement): the tree REVIEW read; graded when REVIEW ran or
#              when AUDIT ran without a fix1 snapshot
#   fix1       the FIX1 snapshot: the tree AUDIT read; graded when AUDIT ran
#   base       the task fixture: the baseline for regression_command (and, refactor,
#              the suite-green-at-base check)
# A snapshot is extracted with `git bundle unbundle` into a scratch bare repository and

    if not parts or ".." in parts:

    return parts

    """make every parent component of tree/parts a real directory inside tree"""
    cur = tree

        if os.path.islink(cur) or (os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur)):

        if not os.path.isdir(cur):
            os.mkdir(cur)
    return os.path.join(cur, parts[-1])


def copy_tree(src, dst, top_exclude=frozenset()):
    """regular files, directories and symlinks only; caches dropped"""
    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)

            keep.append(d)

            elif stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):

SCRIPT_DIR, REPO_ROOT, DOCKER_DEFAULT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
SPRINT = "sprint-1"
TEST_TIMEOUT_S = 120
EXCLUDE_TOP = {".git", ".claude", "CLAUDE.md", ".loa.config.yaml", "grimoires", ".run", ".beads", ".eval", "pr"}
EXCLUDE_ANY = {"__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"}
PHASE_ORDER = ["PLAN", "BARE", "IMPLEMENT", "REVIEW", "FIX1", "AUDIT", "FIX2"]


class GradeError(Exception):
    pass


def die(msg):

    sys.exit(2)


ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ablation-grade.sh", add_help=False)
ap.add_argument("run_dir", nargs="?")
ap.add_argument("task_id", nargs="?")
ap.add_argument("--suite-root")
ap.add_argument("--tasks-dir", choices=["tasks", "smoke"])

def run(cmd, **kw):

def load_yaml(path):
    p = run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path])
    if p.returncode != 0:

    try:

    except ValueError:
        raise GradeError(f"task yaml does not parse: {path}")


def read_json(path):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None


def is_within(path, root):
    path, root = os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root)
    return path == root or path.startswith(root + os.sep)


def remove_path(p):
    if os.path.islink(p) or os.path.isfile(p):
        os.unlink(p)
    elif os.path.isdir(p):
        for r, ds, _fs in os.walk(p):
            for d in ds:
                try:
                    os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700)
                except OSError:
                    pass
        shutil.rmtree(p)
    elif os.path.lexists(p):
        os.unlink(p)


def safe_rel(rel):
    if not isinstance(rel, str) or not rel or rel.startswith("/") or "\\" in rel:
        return None
    parts = [x for x in rel.split("/") if x not in ("", ".")]
    if not parts or ".." in parts:
        return None
    return parts


def ensure_parent(tree, parts):
    """make every parent component of tree/parts a real directory inside tree"""
    cur = tree
    for comp in parts[:-1]:
        cur = os.path.join(cur, comp)
        if os.path.islink(cur) or (os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur)):
            os.unlink(cur)
        if not os.path.isdir(cur):
            os.mkdir(cur)
    return os.path.join(cur, parts[-1])


def copy_tree(src, dst, top_exclude=frozenset()):
    """regular files, directories and symlinks only; caches dropped"""
    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src, followlinks=False):
        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
        keep = []
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            if (rel == "." and d in top_exclude) or d in EXCLUDE_ANY:
                continue
            sp = os.path.join(root, d)
            dp = os.path.join(dst, rel, d)
            if os.path.islink(sp):
                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
                continue
            os.makedirs(dp, exist_ok=True)
            keep.append(d)
        dirs[:] = keep
        for f in sorted(files):
            if rel == "." and f in top_exclude:
                continue
            sp, dp = os.path.join(root, f), os.path.join(dst, rel, f)
            st = os.lstat(sp)
            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
            elif stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
                shutil.copyfile(sp, dp)
                os.chmod(dp, (st.st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)

    parts = safe_rel(rel)
    if parts is None:
        raise GradeError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
    dst = ensure_parent(tree, parts)
    if os.path.lexists(dst):

    if os.path.isdir(src) and not os.path.islink(src):
        copy_tree(src, dst)
    else:
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
        os.chmod(dst, (os.stat(src).st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ task loading
class Task:
    pass


def load_task(task_yaml, suite_root):
    t = Task()
    t.yaml = os.path.abspath(task_yaml)
    t.dir = os.path.dirname(t.yaml)
    t.suite_root = os.path.abspath(suite_root)
    t.spec = load_yaml(t.yaml)
    if not isinstance(t.spec, dict):

    t.type = t.spec.get("type") or ""
    if t.type not in ("bug-fix", "feature-build", "refactor", "review-catch"):
        raise GradeError(f"unknown task type: {t.type!r}")

    95	def changed_files(repo, parent, sha):

    97	    items = raw.split("\0")
    98	    files = []
    99	    i = 0

   107	def numstat(repo, parent, sha, paths=None):
   108	    args = ["diff", "--no-renames", "--numstat", parent, sha]

   111	    rows = []

   118	def blob(repo, commit, path):
   119	    """(mode, bytes) of path at commit, or None when absent."""
   120	    ls = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path).split("\0")[0]
   121	    if not ls:
   122	        return None
   123	    meta, _ = ls.split("\t", 1)
   124	    mode, kind, obj = meta.split()
   125	    if kind != "blob":
   126	        return None
   127	    return mode, git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", obj, binary=True)

   131	    args = ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", commit]
   132	    if prefix:
   133	        args += ["--", prefix]
   134	    return [p for p in git(repo, *args).split("\0") if p]

   141	    dest = os.path.join(root, rel)

   147	def put_from(repo, commit, rel, root, dest_rel=None):
   148	    b = blob(repo, commit, rel)

   154	    write_file(root, dest_rel or rel, data)

   158	def helper_files(repo, commit, test_paths):
   159	    """Test infrastructure the tests rely on: conftest.py up to the root, helpers in each test dir, root runner configs."""
   160	    have = set(tree_files(repo, commit))
   161	    found = set()
   162	    for t in test_paths:

   164	        parts = d.split("/") if d else []
   165	        for i in range(len(parts) + 1):
   166	            c = "/".join(parts[:i] + ["conftest.py"])
   167	            if c in have:
   168	                found.add(c)

   171	                base = os.path.basename(f)
   172	                if base in ("conftest.py", "__init__.py") or base.endswith(".bash") or "helper" in base:
   173	                    found.add(f)

   180	def sibling_files(repo, commit, sources, roots, exclude):
   181	    """The other non-test files in each touched source file's directory (the modules it most likely imports)."""
   182	    dirs = {os.path.dirname(p) for p in sources}

   186	                and not mount_owned(f) and under_roots(f, roots):

   191	def counts(output, runner):
   192	    if runner == "bats":
   193	        passed = len(re.findall(r"^ok ", output, re.M))
   194	        failed = len(re.findall(r"^not ok ", output, re.M))
   195	        return passed, failed
   196	    tail = output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else ""
   197	    num = lambda w: sum(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"(\d+) " + w, tail))
   198	    return num("passed"), num("failed") + num("errors?")

   294	def classify(mode, repo, sha, parents, roots):
   295	    """('candidate', files) | ('refused', path) | ('skipped', reason)."""
   296	    if len(parents) != 1:
   297	        return "skipped", "not a single-parent commit"
   298	    files = changed_files(repo, parents[0], sha)
   299	    for _, p in files:
   300	        if not safe_path(p):
   301	            return "refused", "unsafe path " + json.dumps(p)
   302	    for _, p in files:
   303	        if mount_owned(p):
   304	            return "refused", p
   305	    for _, p in files:
   306	        if not under_roots(p, roots):
   307	            return "skipped", f"outside the allowed roots: {p}"
   308	    for a, d, p in numstat(repo, parents[0], sha):
   309	        if a == "-" or d == "-":
   310	            return "skipped", f"binary change: {p}"
   311	    tests = [p for _, p in files if is_test(p)]
   312	    sources = [p for _, p in files if not is_test(p)]
   313	    if mode == "bugfix":
   314	        if not tests:
   315	            return "skipped", "no test file touched"
   316	        if not sources:
   317	            return "skipped", "no source file touched"
   318	        added_or_modified = [p for s, p in files if is_test(p) and s in "AM"]
   319	        runners = {runner_of(p) for p in added_or_modified} - {None}
   320	        if not runners:
   321	            return "skipped", "no runnable test file (test_*.py, *_test.py, *.bats) added or changed"
   322	        if len(runners) > 1:
   323	            return "skipped", "mixed test runners (pytest and bats)"
   324	    else:
   325	        if tests:
   326	            return "skipped", f"touches a test file: {tests[0]}"
   327	        if len(sources) < 2:
   328	            return "skipped", f"touches {len(sources)} source file(s), want at least 2"
   329	    return "candidate", files

   342	def covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots):

   251	def sanitise(text, stems):
   252	    """Agent-facing text from a commit subject: no control characters, paths, file names, test names, grader words."""
   253	    text = "".join(c if c.isprintable() else " " for c in text)

   256	        if "/" in w or re.search(r"\.(py|sh|bats|js|ts|mjs|json|ya?ml|md|toml|cfg|ini|txt|patch)\b", w) \
   257	                or re.match(r"[\W]*test_\w+", w) or "hidden" in w.lower() \

   294	def classify(mode, repo, sha, parents, roots):
   295	    """('candidate', files) | ('refused', path) | ('skipped', reason)."""
   296	    if len(parents) != 1:
   297	        return "skipped", "not a single-parent commit"
   298	    files = changed_files(repo, parents[0], sha)
   299	    for _, p in files:
   300	        if not safe_path(p):
   301	            return "refused", "unsafe path " + json.dumps(p)
   302	    for _, p in files:
   303	        if mount_owned(p):
   304	            return "refused", p
   305	    for _, p in files:
   306	        if not under_roots(p, roots):
   307	            return "skipped", f"outside the allowed roots: {p}"
   308	    for a, d, p in numstat(repo, parents[0], sha):
   309	        if a == "-" or d == "-":
   310	            return "skipped", f"binary change: {p}"
   311	    tests = [p for _, p in files if is_test(p)]
   312	    sources = [p for _, p in files if not is_test(p)]
   313	    if mode == "bugfix":
   314	        if not tests:
   315	            return "skipped", "no test file touched"
   316	        if not sources:
   317	            return "skipped", "no source file touched"
   318	        added_or_modified = [p for s, p in files if is_test(p) and s in "AM"]
   319	        runners = {runner_of(p) for p in added_or_modified} - {None}
   320	        if not runners:
   321	            return "skipped", "no runnable test file (test_*.py, *_test.py, *.bats) added or changed"
   322	        if len(runners) > 1:
   323	            return "skipped", "mixed test runners (pytest and bats)"
   324	    else:
   325	        if tests:
   326	            return "skipped", f"touches a test file: {tests[0]}"
   327	        if len(sources) < 2:
   328	            return "skipped", f"touches {len(sources)} source file(s), want at least 2"
   329	    return "candidate", files

   342	def covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots):
   343	    """Test files at parent (under the roots) that name a touched source file."""
   344	    names = set()
   345	    for s in sources:
   346	        base = os.path.basename(s)
   347	        names.add(base)
   348	        if base.endswith(".py"):
   349	            names.add(base[:-3])
   350	    pats = [re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])") for n in sorted(names)]
   351	    hits = []
   352	    for r in roots:
   353	        for f in tree_files(repo, parent, r):
   354	            if not is_test(f) or runner_of(f) is None or not safe_path(f) or mount_owned(f):
   355	                continue
   356	            b = blob(repo, parent, f)
   357	            if b is None or b[0] == "120000":
   358	                continue
   359	            text = b[1].decode("utf-8", "replace")
   360	            if any(p.search(text) for p in pats):
   361	                hits.append(f)
   362	    return sorted(set(hits))[:MAX_COVERING_TESTS]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 259 Task 2.2 (SDD §5.14,
     4	# sprint AC-2.9)
     5	#
     6	# seed-bugfix-tasks.sh over a throwaway git repo: a clean fix commit (a Python
     7	# module + its test, red at the parent, green at the commit) becomes a task
     8	# whose every field validates; a fix touching .claude/ is refused by name and
     9	# writes nothing; --dry-run writes nothing; a fix whose test is already green
    10	# at the parent fails its proof (exit 1, nothing written); a fix outside the
    11	# allowed roots is skipped; usage errors are exit 2.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	setup() {
    15	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    16	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    17	  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-bugfix-tasks.sh"
    18	  VS="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh"
    19	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sb.XXXXXX")"
    20	  G="$T/repo"; S="$T/suite"
    21	  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
    22	  python3 -m pytest --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "pytest not importable by python3"
    23	  git init -q -b main "$G"
    24	  mkdir -p "$G/tools/mathx/tests" "$G/docs"
    25	  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
    26	def round_half(x):
    27	    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
    28	    return int(x + 0.5)
    29	PY
    30	  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/conftest.py" <<'PY'
    31	import os, sys
    32	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
    33	PY
    34	  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'
    35	from rounding import round_half
    36	
    37	def test_positive():
    38	    assert round_half(2.5) == 3
    39	PY
    40	  echo "notes" > "$G/docs/README"
    41	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "chore: initial"
    42	}
    43	
    44	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    45	
    46	gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }
    47	
    48	# the clean fix: negative halves round away from zero; two new test cases
    49	commit_clean_fix() {
    50	  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
    51	import math
    52	
    53	
    54	def round_half(x):
    55	    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
    56	    return int(math.copysign(math.floor(abs(x) + 0.5), x))
    57	PY
    58	  cat >> "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'
    59	
    60	def test_negative_half():
    61	    assert round_half(-2.5) == -3
    62	
    63	def test_negative():
    64	    assert round_half(-1.6) == -2
    65	PY
    66	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix(mathx): negative halves round away from zero"
    67	}
    68	
    69	commit_claude_fix() {
    70	  mkdir -p "$G/.claude"
    71	  echo 'echo hi' > "$G/.claude/x.sh"
    72	  printf '\ndef test_again():\n    assert round_half(1.5) == 2\n' >> "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py"
    73	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix: the framework hook"
    74	}
    75	
    76	@test "SB-1 a clean fix commit becomes a task: fixture from the parent, hidden tests from the commit, proof printed, validate-suite passes" {
    77	  commit_clean_fix
    78	  FIX="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)"; BASE="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~1)"
    79	  run "$SEED" --since 2000-01-01 --select 4 --out "$S" --repo "$G"
    80	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    81	  grep -q "^candidate ${FIX:0:12} " <<<"$output"
    82	  grep -qx "proof bugfix-01 ${FIX:0:12}: red 2 failed / green 3 passed" <<<"$output"
    83	  grep -q 'selected 1, written 1, proof failed 0' <<<"$output"
    84	  D="$S/tasks/bugfix-01"
    85	  # fixture = the parent's module, the base test, the conftest; nothing else, no history
    86	  [ "$(cd "$D/fixture" && find . -type f | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "./tools/mathx/rounding.py ./tools/mathx/tests/conftest.py ./tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py " ]
    87	  grep -q 'int(x + 0.5)' "$D/fixture/tools/mathx/rounding.py"
    88	  [ ! -e "$D/fixture/.git" ]
    89	  # hidden = the commit's test + manifest + the non-test diff
    90	  grep -q 'test_negative_half' "$D/hidden/tests/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py"
    91	  [ "$(jq -c . "$D/hidden/manifest.json")" = '{"files":[{"src":"tests/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py","dest":"tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py"}]}' ]
    92	  grep -q '^--- a/tools/mathx/rounding.py' "$D/hidden/reference.patch"
    93	  ! grep -q 'test_rounding' "$D/hidden/reference.patch" || false
    94	  # every field
    95	  [ "$(yq -r .type "$D/task.yaml")" = "bug-fix" ]
    96	  [ "$(yq -r .source.kind "$D/task.yaml")" = "loa-history" ]
    97	  [ "$(yq -r .source.fix_commit "$D/task.yaml")" = "$FIX" ]
    98	  [ "$(yq -r .source.base_commit "$D/task.yaml")" = "$BASE" ]
    99	  [ "$(yq -r .source.date "$D/task.yaml")" = "$(git -C "$G" log -1 --format=%cs "$FIX")" ]
   100	  [ "$(yq -r .fixture "$D/task.yaml")" = "tasks/bugfix-01/fixture" ]

     8	# churn recorded (task.yaml source.churn and the printed churn line, equal to
     9	# git diff --numstat), the suite green at both ends, the structural check left
    10	# to author; a candidate touching a test file is skipped with the reason; one
    11	# touching grimoires/ is refused by name; a one-file change is skipped;
    12	# --dry-run writes nothing; a refactor that breaks the suite fails its proof.
    13	# =============================================================================
    14	
    15	setup() {
    16	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    17	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

    24	  git init -q -b main "$G"
    25	  mkdir -p "$G/tools/fmt/tests"
    26	  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/left.py" <<'PY'
    27	def left(s, width):
    28	    s = str(s)
    29	    if len(s) >= width:
    30	        return s
    31	    return s + " " * (width - len(s))
    32	PY
    33	  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/right.py" <<'PY'
    34	def right(s, width):
    35	    s = str(s)
    36	    if len(s) >= width:
    37	        return s
    38	    return " " * (width - len(s)) + s
    39	PY
    40	  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/tests/conftest.py" <<'PY'
    41	import os, sys
    42	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
    43	PY

    45	from left import left
    46	from right import right
    47	
    48	def test_left():
    49	    assert left("ab", 4) == "ab  "
    50	    assert left("abcde", 4) == "abcde"
    51	
    52	def test_right():
    53	    assert right(7, 3) == "  7"
    54	PY
    55	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "chore: initial"
    56	}

    66	    return " " * max(0, width - len(str(s)))
    67	PY

    69	  printf 'from pad import gap\n\n\ndef right(s, width):\n    return gap(s, width) + str(s)\n' > "$G/tools/fmt/right.py"

# rf-py: a refactor (total() must reuse add()); the suite is green at both ends
make_rf_py() {
  local d="$S/tasks/rf-py" w="$T/w-rf"
  mkdir -p "$d/fixture/src/calc" "$d/fixture/tests" "$d/hidden/tests" "$d/hidden/structural"
  : > "$d/fixture/src/calc/__init__.py"
  printf 'def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n\n\ndef total(xs):\n    s = 0\n    for x in xs:\n        s = s + x\n    return s\n' > "$d/fixture/src/calc/ops.py"
  printf 'import os, sys\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "src"))\n' > "$d/fixture/conftest.py"
  printf 'from calc.ops import add, total\n\n\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n\n\ndef test_total():\n    assert total([1, 2, 3]) == 6\n' > "$d/hidden/tests/test_ops.py"
  printf 'import inspect\nfrom calc import ops\n\n\ndef test_total_reuses_add():\n    assert "add(" in inspect.getsource(ops.total)\n' > "$d/hidden/structural/test_structure.py"
  echo '{"files": [{"src": "tests/test_ops.py", "dest": "tests/test_ops.py"}, {"src": "structural/test_structure.py", "dest": "structural/test_structure.py"}]}' > "$d/hidden/manifest.json"
  mkdir -p "$w/a" "$w/b"; cp -a "$d/fixture/." "$w/a/"; cp -a "$d/fixture/." "$w/b/"
  printf 'def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n\n\ndef total(xs):\n    s = 0\n    for x in xs:\n        s = add(s, x)\n    return s\n' > "$w/b/src/calc/ops.py"
  (cd "$w" && diff -ruN a b > "$d/hidden/reference.patch" || true)
  printf 'Make total reuse add.\n' > "$d/TASK.md"
  cat > "$d/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: rf-py
schema_version: 1
type: refactor
fixture: tasks/rf-py/fixture
criterion: "the sum reuses the pairwise helper"
test_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests"]
regression_command: null
reference_patch: hidden/reference.patch
grader_protected: [conftest.py]
structural_check: hidden/structural/test_structure.py
review_catch: null
suite_version: 1
YAML
}

# rc-x: a review-catch task over a 30-line PR with a high and a low defect
make_rc() {
  local d="$S/tasks/rc-x" p="$T/prs/pr-77" i
  mkdir -p "$d" "$p/base/lib" "$p/head/lib" "$T/manifests"
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do echo "line_$i=1"; done > "$p/base/lib/x.sh"
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do echo "line_$i=2"; done > "$p/head/lib/x.sh"
  printf -- '--- a/lib/x.sh\n+++ b/lib/x.sh\n' > "$p/head.diff"
  printf '# PR\n' > "$p/PR.md"
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-77.json" <<'EOF'
{"fixture": "pr-77", "defects": [
  {"id": "D01-overflow-guard-dropped", "file": "lib/x.sh", "anchor_line": 5, "severity": "high", "category": "logic"},
  {"id": "D02-unquoted-expansion", "file": "lib/x.sh", "anchor_line": 20, "severity": "low", "category": "logic"}]}
EOF
  printf 'Review the pull request.\n' > "$d/TASK.md"
  cat > "$d/task.yaml" <<YAML
id: rc-x
schema_version: 1
type: review-catch
fixture: null
criterion: "review the change"
test_command: null
regression_command: null
reference_patch: null
grader_protected: []
structural_check: null
review_catch: {fixture: "$p", manifest: "$T/manifests/pr-77.json"}
suite_version: 1
YAML
}

sg() { local rd="$1"; shift; git -C "$rd/sandbox" -c user.email=e@l -c user.name=eval -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }

# make_run <task-id> <run-dir>: the task fixture (or the PR under pr/) committed as base
make_run() {
  local id="$1" rd="$2" td="$S/tasks/$1"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox" "$rd/snapshots" "$rd/transcripts" "$rd/eval" "$rd/meta"
  echo "$id" > "$rd.task"   # beside the run dir, for apply_ref
  if [[ -d "$td/fixture" ]]; then cp -a "$td/fixture/." "$rd/sandbox/"
  else mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/pr"; cp -a "$T/prs/pr-77/." "$rd/sandbox/pr/"; fi
  sg "$rd" init -q
  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$rd/sandbox/.git/info/exclude"
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m base
  jq -n --arg b "$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)" '{base: $b}' > "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1" "$rd/sandbox/.claude"
  echo "# mount" > "$rd/sandbox/CLAUDE.md"
  printf '{"run_id": "r-%s", "status": "completed", "arm": "a1_full"}\n' "$id" > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
  echo a1_full > "$rd/meta/arm"
}
# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
snap() {
  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
}
# verdict <run-dir> review|audit <VERDICT> [body]
verdict() {
  local f=engineer-feedback.md; [[ "$2" == audit ]] && f=auditor-sprint-feedback.md
  printf '# Feedback\n\n%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1}} -->\n' "${4:-}" "$2" "$3" \
    > "$1/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/$f"
}
apply_ref() { patch -s -p1 -d "$1/sandbox" < "$S/tasks/$(cat "$1.task")/hidden/reference.patch"; }
# tool_use <run-dir> <LABEL> <tool> <input-json>: one assistant tool_use event line
tool_use() {
  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \
    >> "$1/transcripts/events-$2.jsonl"
}
grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
tree_digest() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, os, sys
h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
    ds.sort()
    for n in sorted(ds + fs):

sg() { local rd="$1"; shift; git -C "$rd/sandbox" -c user.email=e@l -c user.name=eval -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }

# make_run <task-id> <run-dir>: the task fixture (or the PR under pr/) committed as base
make_run() {
  local id="$1" rd="$2" td="$S/tasks/$1"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox" "$rd/snapshots" "$rd/transcripts" "$rd/eval" "$rd/meta"
  echo "$id" > "$rd.task"   # beside the run dir, for apply_ref
  if [[ -d "$td/fixture" ]]; then cp -a "$td/fixture/." "$rd/sandbox/"
  else mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/pr"; cp -a "$T/prs/pr-77/." "$rd/sandbox/pr/"; fi
  sg "$rd" init -q
  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$rd/sandbox/.git/info/exclude"
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m base
  jq -n --arg b "$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)" '{base: $b}' > "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1" "$rd/sandbox/.claude"
  echo "# mount" > "$rd/sandbox/CLAUDE.md"
  printf '{"run_id": "r-%s", "status": "completed", "arm": "a1_full"}\n' "$id" > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
  echo a1_full > "$rd/meta/arm"
}
# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
snap() {
  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
}
# verdict <run-dir> review|audit <VERDICT> [body]
verdict() {
  local f=engineer-feedback.md; [[ "$2" == audit ]] && f=auditor-sprint-feedback.md
  printf '# Feedback\n\n%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1}} -->\n' "${4:-}" "$2" "$3" \
    > "$1/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/$f"
}
apply_ref() { patch -s -p1 -d "$1/sandbox" < "$S/tasks/$(cat "$1.task")/hidden/reference.patch"; }
# tool_use <run-dir> <LABEL> <tool> <input-json>: one assistant tool_use event line
tool_use() {
  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \
    >> "$1/transcripts/events-$2.jsonl"
}
grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
tree_digest() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, os, sys
h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
    ds.sort()
    for n in sorted(ds + fs):
        p = os.path.join(r, n); h.update(os.path.relpath(p, root).encode() + b"\0")
        if os.path.islink(p): h.update(b"L" + os.readlink(p).encode())
        elif os.path.isfile(p): h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
print(h.hexdigest())' "$1"
}

head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16 — BATS_BIN is hard-coded to a developer's personal dotfiles bats (`$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats`) and symlinked as the image's `bats` stand-in. On CI or any other machine the symlink dangles, so every bats-graded case (bf-sh in AG-2/AG-7, the smoke self-checks) fails. The repo already guards against this pattern: pipeline-run.bats asserts fingerprint.sh carries no `dotfiles` path and uses LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN. Resolve bats through `command -v bats`/LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN and skip when it is absent.
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:86 — `git log --since=YYYY-MM-DD` uses git's approxidate, which keeps the current time of day for a date-only value. Commits made on DATE before the clock time of the run are silently dropped (checked: with --since=2026-08-01 run at 08:40, a commit at 2026-08-01 00:30 is excluded and one at 23:30 is kept). This breaks the documented "committer date is on or after it" contract and makes candidate selection depend on the wall clock. Pass `--since=<DATE>T00:00:00` (or filter on %cs in Python).
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:570 — `selected = cands[:a.select]` is fixed before any task is built. A candidate that build_refactor later skips ("no test at the parent names a touched file", "covering tests mix pytest and bats") or that the no-secrets scan refuses still uses up a selection slot, so fewer than N tasks get written even when more candidates exist. Both wrapper headers say these outcomes do not count (seed-refactor-tasks.sh:38, seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:43). Iterate over all candidates until N tasks are written or N proofs have failed.
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:397 — test_command runs whole test directories (test_dirs) rather than the hidden test files. TASK.md tells the agent to add a regression test of its own, and anything it adds under that directory is then counted in the grader's `hidden_tests` passed/total and failed_names (ablation-grade.sh runs test_command on the final tree, and AG-1 already shows the fixture's own tests in the "hidden" 7/7). Agent-written tests inflate the hidden pass rate, and a broken agent test reads as a hidden-test failure. Name the hidden test files (the manifest dests) in test_command.
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:213 — the proof output is `stdout + stderr`, and counts() (line 196) parses only the very last line of that text as the pytest summary. Any stderr output (an interpreter-shutdown warning, "Exception ignored…", a plugin notice) becomes the last line, so passed and failed both read 0. A real fix then fails as "not red at base" or "not green at reference", and the proof outcome depends on noise. Parse stdout on its own, or search for the summary line instead of taking the tail.
head/evals/tests/validate-suite.bats:41 — PR.md says the change adds sixteen frozen-suite tasks under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks/, but the diff contains no grimoires/ file. At the same time VS-1 changes from pinned expectations ("2 task(s) valid", exactly 4 counts lines, exit 1) to values computed from whatever is on disk, so it passes whether the sixteen tasks exist or not and can no longer detect a missing or partial suite. Either commit the tasks and pin the expected count (16 tasks plus the smoke tasks, 0 counts lines), or correct the description.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md` with six findings and the verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I reviewed by reading the code. I reproduced one finding (the `--since` date handling) in a throwaway git repo, but I didn't run the PR's bats suites.

**Blocking:**
1. **`evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16`**: the test's `bats` comes from a fixed path in one developer's personal dotfiles (`$HOME/.local/dotfiles/...`). On CI or any other machine that path doesn't exist, so every bats-based grading test fails. The repo already guards against this elsewhere: `pipeline-run.bats` checks that no `dotfiles` path appears and uses `LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` instead.
2. **`evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:86`**: `git log --since=YYYY-MM-DD` treats the date as that day at the current clock time. Commits made earlier on the start date are silently dropped, which contradicts the documented "on or after" behaviour. In my test, a commit at 00:30 on the start date was excluded and one at 23:30 was kept.
3. **`evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:570`**: the `--select N` list is fixed before any task is built. Commits skipped or refused later still use up a slot, so fewer than N tasks get written. Both seeder scripts' help text says those commits don't count.
4. **`evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:397`**: the test command runs whole test directories rather than just the hidden test files. Any regression test the agent writes (which the task brief asks for) is counted in the grader's "hidden tests" score. A passing agent test inflates the score, and a broken one counts as a hidden-test failure.

**Lower severity:**
5. **`evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:213`/`196`**: the seeder reads the pytest summary from the last line of combined stdout and stderr. Any stray stderr output makes it read 0 passed and 0 failed, so a valid fix can fail its proof.
6. **`evals/tests/validate-suite.bats:41`**: the PR description says it adds sixteen frozen-suite tasks, but the diff contains no `grimoires/` files. The VS-1 test was also changed to compute its expected counts from whatever is on disk, so it can no longer catch a missing or partial suite.

The other parts of the diff look correct. The regenerated `pr-14.json`/`pr-15.json` manifests match `SHA256SUMS`, and no generated-file paths are left in either manifest's fix regions. The `source.churn` validation and the docker-stub change are also fine.
